label: UniFi Gateway Max
description: Five 2.5GbE ports and 2.3 Gbps of IDS/IPS throughput, with a 2.5G WAN and four LAN ports. The gateway for a 2.5G access network that needs real inspection.
notes:
Vendor figures read 2026-11-19 from techspecs.ui.com/unifi/cloud-gateways/uxg-max (HTTP 200, 647,803 B): Port Layout = 2.5 GbE RJ45 x5 (2.5G/1G/100M/10M), Max. WAN Port Count 4, Default WAN Ports (1) 2.5 GbE RJ45, IDS/IPS Throughput 2.3 Gbps, Form Factor compact desktop, Max. Power Consumption 9.6 W, Power Method = USB type C (5V DC/3A), Supported Voltage Range 100-240V AC, Heat Dissipation 33 BTU/hr. One port is the WAN and the remaining four are LAN; the ports are assignable, so they are modelled as five symmetric 2.5G interfaces.
Power: USB-C 5 V/3 A adapter, no PoE input published. store.ui.com/us/en/products/uxg-max (HTTP 200, 525,162 B): PoE Budget flag Empty, Power Method "USB type C (5V DC/3A)", Max. PoE Wattage per Port by PSE Empty. All five copper ports therefore say poeIn: false, or isPoePd()'s "unifi" match would put a 12.95 W draw on each of them - 64.75 W against a switch budget for a gateway on a 5 V wall wart. Same correction as uxg-pro.json (PR #2118). Trap: dl.ui.com/ds/uxg-max_ds.pdf lands on the 609,911-byte techspecs front page, not a datasheet.

LAN bank is one bridge (measured 2026-11-20 23:5x UTC). Two Ubiquiti surfaces print a bridge table for this SKU: `https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/cloud-gateways/uxg-max` (HTTP 200, 647,803 B) gives **MAC Address Table Size = 2,000** under Networking beside `Port Layout - 2.5 GbE RJ45 = 5 (2.5G/1G/100M/10M)`, and `https://store.ui.com/us/en/products/uxg-max` (HTTP 200, 525,294 B) repeats the 2,000 row while flagging both **VLAN/Subnet-based Traffic Segmentation** and **LACP Port Aggregation** as Empty - so neither tagging nor bundling is claimed, and the token is read for what it is: MAC learning + flooding. With the row lacking `l2-forward`, the four LAN ports were four routed interfaces: `switchport access vlan` answered "cannot switch frames" and two hosts on eth1/eth2 in 192.168.1.0/24 could not ARP each other. `no switchport` still routes a port; all five ports keep their 2.5G rate and the default WAN is unchanged.
